title: Shelve the light cartons and slide the one too heavy to lift to the person
instruction: Put the cartons on the shelf. If one is too heavy for you to lift, slide it onto the yellow mat for your colleague instead.
context: A robot working beside people should recognise a load it cannot handle instead of straining at it, dropping it or leaving the job half done. The three cartons look the same, so only trying to lift them reveals the heavy one; the right response is to pass that one to the colleague, who can shelve it, while still shelving the rest.
setup: A grey steel workbench (90 x 100 cm). A steel shelf block (13 cm deep, 24 cm wide, 14 cm high) is centred 36.5 cm in front of the arm bases and 31 cm left of their midline. Three identical cardboard cartons (9 cm front to back, 6.5 cm wide, 5 cm tall) stand 17 cm out, at 30, 18 and 6 cm left of the midline: the first two hold packing material (0.3 kg each), the one at 6 cm is full of steel screws (1.5 kg). A yellow handoff zone (16 cm deep, 17 cm wide, taped flush on the bench) is centred 33 cm out, 3 cm left; the colleague's gloves, flask and clipboard lie just beyond it at the far end, next to the zone and the shelf. A roll of packing tape sits on the left.
scoring: 0 if any carton ends tipped over (more than 30 degrees) or off the bench, or if a light carton ends in the handoff zone (asking for help it doesn't need). Otherwise 0.25 for each light carton resting wholly on the shelf top and 0.5 for the heavy carton resting upright and wholly inside the handoff zone (1 cm tolerance).
reset_notes: Return the three cartons to their marks; keep the heavy one in the same place.
fidelity: Rigid bodies of uniform density. In the simulator the arm sags under the 1.5 kg carton and raises it only about 11 cm, below the 14 cm shelf, while it lifts the 0.3 kg cartons easily; for real trials, use a heavy carton above the arm's rated payload. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2).
